title: The Day the Clocks Gossiped
skyStory: The moon is a fifth full and floating lazily in Pisces, the sign of tides and strange little signs. Pisces has been fiddling with every clock between the cabin and the shore, nudging digits around like fridge magnets. It is not malicious. It just thinks numbers should tell stories. Saturn, guardian of time, is furious. Also, secretly, impressed.

reading: Watch the clocks today. At some point you will glance at your phone and it will read 12:22, the exact date of Nancy's solstice birthday. Then it will happen again on a microwave, a parking sign, a page number. The universe is not subtle and has never claimed to be.

Meanwhile, over on the shore, Nancy will keep seeing 3:21, your equinox birthday. DES, in both directions at once. [[The Star]] is winking from either end of the line. Send your best sighting at the exact minute the next one happens, if you can manage the timing. Mars says you cannot. Prove Mars wrong.
joel.mission: Screenshot every 12:22 you see today and send Nancy the full collection at bedtime.
joel.omen: A clock running exactly one minute fast. It means you are slightly ahead of schedule on something you were fretting about.

reading: Your sharp Wood Rat eyes will catch it first: 3:21 on the oven clock. Joel's birthday, March 21, staring at you from the kitchen. You will shrug it off. Then it appears again on a bus, then on a page number, then on a clock in a shop window.

Don't even scream. Fine, maybe scream a tiny bit into a scarf. Over at the cabin, Joel is getting 12:22 on repeat, your solstice birthday, at the same time. [[Temperance]] pours the numbers back and forth between two cups. Text him the moment your third 3:21 shows up, and watch how fast he replies.
nancy.mission: Count every 3:21 you see today on your fingers, and send Joel the final total with maximum drama.
nancy.omen: A bus or truck with 321 in its number. It means the friendship is broadcasting loud and clear today.

together.text: Tonight, compare your counts. Whoever saw the other's birthday number more times picks the next shared mission. In case of a tie, you both must say ΔΕΣ out loud at 9:21 pm, which is neither birthday but feels close enough.
